data.name: Nrusingha
data.gender_notes: Nrusingha is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: Nrsi + Ishvara: God in human form
data.long_meaning: Nrsi: Lord Narasimha, a form of Vishnu; Ishvara: God in human form. Narasimha is a manifestation of Vishnu, who saved the world from a demon, Hiranyakashipu. He appeared in a half-lion, half-human form to protect his devotee, Prahlada. The name Nrusingha signifies God appearing in human form for the protection and salvation of His devotees.
data.spiritual_meaning: Divine protection and salvation in human form
data.etymology: Nrusingha belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Nrsi + Ishvara: God in human form.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nrusingha total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Nrusingha' holds cultural importance in Hinduism as it signifies the belief in the divine intervention in human life. Lord Narasimha, a powerful and popular form of Vishnu, represents not only strength and vigor but also love and compassion towards devotees. The name is a reminder of the protectiveness and salvage capabilities of deities, imparting a sense of hope and faith among the followers.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name 'Nrusingha' emphasizes the power of the divine to come down to the human realm and provide protection and guidance. It conveys the idea that God is not just an abstract concept but a living force who can be embraced and sought refuge in during times of need. The name offers a sense of comfort, security, and brings a deep sense of connection to the divine presence.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nrusingha represents the divine form of Lord Vishnu, who is guardian of dharma (cosmic order) and protector against evil. This form embodies the fierce and powerful aspect of Vishnu, ready to annihilate Adharma (disorder) and uphold righteousness.

name_in_real_life.story: Lakshmi Nrusingha, a teacher in Kolkata, India, shares that their name Nrusingha meaning "Nrsi + Ishvara: God in human form" has been a constant source of inspiration, motivating them to follow Hindu values and serve their community.
